reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The new missing-key and empty-config tests can fail when provider keys remain in $_ENV or $_SERVER because the callbacks only unset the process environment.
1 open issue - [Clear superglobal entries when testing unset environment keys](https://github.com/LLPhant/LLPhant/pull/557#discussion_r4503014922) · New
What changed in this PR This PR prevents LLPhant’s Mistral and Gemini integrations from falling back to OpenAI credentials and makes missing-key errors identify the correct provider. **Changes:** - Use an empty key when provider-specific credentials are unavailable. - Correct Mistral’s error message and add Gemini validation that permits an injected client. - Add regression tests for missing credentials and environments containing only `OPENAI_API_KEY`. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `tests/​Unit/​Chat/​ApiKeyEnvironmentTest.php` | Tests provider-specific errors and prevention of OpenAI key fallback. | | `src/​MistralAIConfig.php` | Blocks fallback to OpenAI credentials. | | `src/​GeminiOpenAIConfig.php` | Blocks fallback to OpenAI credentials. | | `src/​Chat/​MistralAIChat.php` | Names `MISTRAL_API_KEY` in the missing-key error. | | `src/​Chat/​GeminiAIChat.php` | Adds a Gemini-specific missing-key check while allowing injected clients. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: `putenv()` does not clear `$_ENV` or `$_SERVER`, but `Utility::readEnvironment()` falls back to both (`src/Utility.php:36–48`). If a provider key is present in either superglobal, these callbacks still find it despite requesting an unset key, so the new missing-key and empty-config assertions fail in that environment. Snapshot, clear, and restore the named entries in both superglobals as well as the process environment.
